tasks.title: Match the closing bit to the machine
tasks.body:
1. Have the operator identify the start of a production cycle over the phone.
  2. Watch DB98.DBX112.7 and Q44.0. Record when they turn TRUE and whether there is another pulse later in the same cycle.

tasks.title: Match the robot return to cycle end
tasks.body:
1. Watch DB94.DBX29.4 and I505.7. Record the low state and the return to TRUE.
  2. Have the operator confirm whether that return is when the robot is done and clear. Save your photos/times in the notes. Do not mark a robot sequence verified from manual closing alone.

tasks.title: Create the CSI group and choose LAD
tasks.body:
1. Save a separate working copy of the current MM6 project. Under Program blocks, check the names below before creating anything. Do not overwrite an existing CSI block or convert an already-running block in place.
  2. Right-click Program blocks → Add new group; name it CSI if available. Create only new blocks through Add new block; move them into this group.
  3. This route creates CSI_Report and CSI_Setup global DBs; CSI_Increment and CSI_AddElapsed FCs; CSI_PeriodCounter and CSI_Reporting FBs; and CSI_Reporting_DB as the main instance. All four executable blocks use LAD.
  4. If you already built the earlier SCL version, keep that copy. This ladder build has a different FB interface and direct OB1 call. Do not mix the two versions or run both. Previous checks/notes remain under Completed → Earlier checklist records.

Manual ladder specification, not a TIA-compiled or PLC-tested project. Keep the new Enable/WiringReviewed bits FALSE until compilation, input checks and load review are complete.

How to place contacts, boxes and branches

In TIA: open the new LAD block. Tags go in its upper declaration grid; rungs go in the networks below.

  1. To add a rung, right-click the last network heading → Insert network. Put the new network BELOW it and use the exact network title shown here.
  2. Use the toolbar’s Normally open contact, Normally closed contact and Coil. Click a symbol’s tag field and type the tag. Use a normal coil unless the panel specifically says (S) or (R).
  3. For a box: open the Instructions pane on the right. Search its exact name, such as MOVE, ADD, CALCULATE, CONVERT or T_CONV, and drag it into the network. Select the stated data type in its dropdown, then fill the named pins.
  4. For comparisons use Basic instructions → Comparator operations, choose the shown operator and DInt, and enter the two operands shown on either side of the vertical bar.
  5. Use Open branch / Close branch for parallel paths. A network panel is a wiring recipe, NOT text to paste into TIA. Multiple boxes listed as parallel output branches share the condition before their split.
  6. For a reusable block call, drag the named block from Program blocks. A CSI_PeriodCounter call inside CSI_Reporting uses Multi-instance; select the exact existing Static instance named in the panel. Keep its EN on the rail and fill every Input. Its Output pins may remain unwired because later MOVE boxes read those instance members.

tasks.title: Create its instance DB and add one call in OB1
tasks.body:
1. Finish and compile all four new LAD blocks. Under Add new block → Data block, name CSI_Reporting_DB; select CSI_Reporting as its Type, NOT Global DB. Let TIA populate its members.
  2. Open OB1. Keep all existing networks. Add one new network after the current final processing, outside any conditional jump. The analyzed MM6 program ends with RobotMain/FC900 at network 48.
  3. If OB1 is LAD/FBD, drag CSI_Reporting into that empty network and select the existing single-instance CSI_Reporting_DB. Leave EN directly on the rail, with no AUTO contact.
  4. If the existing OB1 is STL, leave its language unchanged. Insert the FB call from Program blocks and select CSI_Reporting_DB. Its call is CALL "CSI_Reporting", "CSI_Reporting_DB"; TIA inserts the five parameter rows. Fill them as below.
  5. Connect CloseCommand to DB98.DBX112.7 and RobotPermit to DB94.DBX29.6. This call does not write either bit. Do not also call the earlier CSI_Run wrapper.
InputConnect to
ProductionEligibleVerified production-to-count condition, excluding setup/jog.
RobotDataValidVerified current/valid robot/input communication condition.
AbortCycleVerified cancellation of the measured cycle. Normal waiting is NOT an abort.

The three conditions above still need verified tags. For OFFLINE compilation only, FALSE / FALSE / TRUE keeps the observer disabled. Do not use permanent TRUE shortcuts or enable it with unresolved inputs.

tasks.title: Set the startup flag without changing the machine sequence
tasks.body:
1. Open the existing standard startup OB, normally OB100, and preserve its code.
  2. Add one final LAD network directly on the rail with a Set coil (S) addressed to "CSI_Setup".StartupPending. No contact is needed.
  3. If the existing startup OB is STL, keep that language: append SET followed by S "CSI_Setup".StartupPending in a new network. If there is no startup OB, add a standard Organization block → Startup in LAD with an unused number.
  4. The last network of CSI_Reporting resets this new bit after handling the first scan. No separate CSI_Startup FC is needed in this ladder route.

tasks.title: Compile and review only the intended additions
tasks.body:
1. Compile the new blocks, then Program blocks → Compile → Software (only changes). Resolve every error before loading. Save the laptop project.
  2. Review retention for the NEW CSI_Report and CSI_Reporting_DB: counts/keys/quality must remain together. Without retention, do not promise history across power loss. If changing retention requires STOP, defer it to an approved window instead of accepting STOP on a running machine.
  3. At the approved commissioning point, choose Download to device → Software (only changes). Inspect Load preview: the new CSI blocks and intended OB additions only.
  4. Cancel unexpected STOP, hardware/F-program changes, deletions, or initialization of existing machine DBs. Keep Enable and WiringReviewed FALSE. A reporting purpose does not make an incorrect download harmless.

tasks.title: Watch the new values, then enable only CSI_Setup
tasks.body:
1. Create a separate reporting watch table. Add the symbolic tags below in Name, or drag members from CSI_Report/CSI_Setup. Click Monitor all. Require SchemaVersion=3, correct local date/time, ClockValid=1 and ConfigurationOK=1.
  2. Verify the three call inputs with the machine. With approval, modify ONLY "CSI_Setup".WiringReviewed and "CSI_Setup".Enable to TRUE. Use normal Modify selected values, not Force. Clear their Modify cells afterward.
  3. State 10 synchronizes through a robot low/high boundary; 20 times a known wait; 30 times the cycle. The first unknown cycle is deliberately skipped. Outside the weekday schedule State=0 and production is not counted.

tasks.title: Check five cycles, the extra pulse and shift hold
tasks.body:
1. Compare five normal cycles with Chris or the operator. Each qualified completion updates PreviousCycleSeconds and increments TotalCompleted once. The secondary close pulse must not restart the stopwatch.
  2. Check live BetweenCycleSeconds while waiting and PreviousBetweenSeconds after the next start. Use BetweenActive and the held Valid flags. CPU STOP/power-off time is not measured by TIME_TCK.
  3. Test weekday boundaries in an isolated test copy or with observed real boundaries, not by changing a running production PLC clock. Confirm Friday day count holds until Monday 06:30 and Thursday-night count until Monday 17:00. Weekend/manual cycles must not update production totals or held cycle time.
  4. Check Partial flags and period keys. A first or interrupted shift can be partial. Archive the verified project and export this checklist’s progress.

tasks.title: Select the existing MM6 device
tasks.body:
1. Open the Kepware server configuration and save a backup of its project.
  2. In the left connection tree, select the existing MM6 device. Confirm its endpoint is MM6, not another machine.
  3. Use the address map here only with the Siemens TCP/IP Ethernet driver. A symbolic S7 Plus or OPC UA connection uses its own addressing. Do not change PLC security or hardware to make a connection work.

tasks.title: Create and test SchemaVersion
tasks.body:
1. Under MM6, right-click → New Tag Group → name it Production. Use the existing group if it is already there.
  2. Select Production → right-click → New Tag. Enter Name = SchemaVersion; Address = the SchemaVersion address in the map below; Data type = Long; Client access = Read Only; Scan rate = 1000 ms. Click Apply/OK.
  3. Open Tools → Launch OPC Quick Client (or the installed test client). Browse the MM6 Production group. Require Good quality and value 3. Stop and check the DB number, driver and access if it is not Good.

tasks.title: Add the time and count tags
tasks.body:
Repeat New Tag for the rows in the address map below. Use Long for DINT counts/status and Float for REAL seconds. Keep every tag Read Only.

Add Heartbeat and compare one time value with TIA before entering the remaining rows. The CSV is an address reference; for bulk import, export one tag from this Kepware version and use its exact CSV format.

tasks.title: Check the display and save Kepware
tasks.body:
1. Compare current/previous hour, day and both shift counts with TIA. Check PreviousCycleSeconds and both between-cycle values.
  2. Use BetweenActive for live waiting, the Valid fields for held values, and Partial/key fields for period quality. Do not display stale/bad-quality data as live.
  3. Save the Kepware project and record the real channel/device/group path. Export this checklist’s progress if you are moving to another computer.

instructions.title: Place a ladder contact, coil or instruction box
instructions.body:
In TIA: open the new LAD block. Tags go in its upper declaration grid; rungs go in the networks below.

  1. To add a rung, right-click the last network heading → Insert network. Put the new network BELOW it and use the exact network title shown here.
  2. Use the toolbar’s Normally open contact, Normally closed contact and Coil. Click a symbol’s tag field and type the tag. Use a normal coil unless the panel specifically says (S) or (R).
  3. For a box: open the Instructions pane on the right. Search its exact name, such as MOVE, ADD, CALCULATE, CONVERT or T_CONV, and drag it into the network. Select the stated data type in its dropdown, then fill the named pins.
  4. For comparisons use Basic instructions → Comparator operations, choose the shown operator and DInt, and enter the two operands shown on either side of the vertical bar.
  5. Use Open branch / Close branch for parallel paths. A network panel is a wiring recipe, NOT text to paste into TIA. Multiple boxes listed as parallel output branches share the condition before their split.
  6. For a reusable block call, drag the named block from Program blocks. A CSI_PeriodCounter call inside CSI_Reporting uses Multi-instance; select the exact existing Static instance named in the panel. Keep its EN on the rail and fill every Input. Its Output pins may remain unwired because later MOVE boxes read those instance members.

instructions.title: Shift times and what holds over the weekend
instructions.body:
Shift 1: Mon–Fri 06:30–17:00. Shift 2: Mon–Thu 17:00 to the next 06:00. Thursday’s night shift includes Friday before 06:00. No Friday-night shift.

Shift Current values hold after ending, then reset only at their own next scheduled start. Previous holds the last closed shift. No completed cycles outside the scheduled windows enter hour/day/shift/total production counts. Held cycle/waiting results are not replaced by weekend runs. The observer resynchronizes when scheduled production resumes.
